selectedOriginals.caption: Belfort van Gent, foto door mezelf genomen vanop de Sint-Baafskathedraal
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full elevated selected original individually inspected: own tower at rear of attached long Cloth Hall, two windows per tower face at three stages, pierced balcony, projecting open gold clock ring before dark pointed bell opening, four polygonal corner turrets/white hourglass shutters, tall slate spire with three tiers of little dormers/gilded crest/copper dragon. Hall eleven facade bays/eleven stepped dormers and eleven small timber dormers per roof slope. Other churches, square stalls, trees and neighbors excluded.

selectedOriginals.caption: The Belfort in Gent.
selectedOriginals.inspection: Full selected2005original individually inspected: pale grey rough tower masonry versus warmer dressed Cloth Hall limestone, dark slate/copper roof, gold skeletal clock before recessed pointed opening, actual pierced balcony, corner turrets and weather poles. Hall facade has low square windows/tall pointed windows with blind upper tracery/small rectangular upper windows/stepped dormers; no flat photographic facade.

additionalInspected.inspection: Full2025spire detail individually inspected: octagonal central slate spire tapers to narrow drum with three projecting cornices, six-ish crown gablets with fine gold rods/open spaces around the drum, slender dark upper spire/gold crochets and dragon. Main spire has three staggered little white/black hourglass dormer tiers, smaller corner turret spires have same shutters and gold finials. Fine gilded ornament proportional, not a measured survey.

additionalInspected.caption: Ghent
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2009clock/balcony close-up individually inspected: two concentric skeletal gold rings, open Roman numeral stroke band and ornate hands over real pointed recessed belfry opening and black grille. Clock is not an opaque disc. Layered pointed stone archivolts, separate pierced balcony trefoil/circle counters and slender posts. No copied lettering or photographic textures.

additionalInspected.caption: 2011-10-23 in Ghent
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2011oblique upper exterior individually inspected: clocks on adjoining faces, polygonal corner turrets from balcony up to slate spires, thin projecting poles at two levels, four watchman silhouettes near balcony corners, three paired tower lancet stages below with center mullion/oculus tracery and shutter/louver variation. Dense fine statuary simplified.

Full2006Mammelokker detail individually inspected: directly attached small entrance annex with curved front gable, concentric curving molding/oval oculus and two small slit-like windows, sculptural central relief, dark slate sloping roofs. Relief represented as restrained abstract paired figures; no fine anatomical replica.

additionalInspected.caption: Belfort van Gent.
additionalInspected.inspection: Full2011monochrome tower exterior individually inspected: three paired pointed window levels above low base, seven stringcourses/large masonry fields, real top clock arch/open balcony, hourglass turret shutters and crop of directly attached Mammelokker entrance at base. Cornice gargoyles and four watchmen retained as original geometric silhouettes.

additionalInspected.caption: Belgique - Gand - Halle aux Draps (Lakenhalle, style gothique, 15e siècle)
additionalInspected.inspection: Full local Cloth Hall original individually inspected: eleven tall facade bays with alternating stepped buttresses, lower rectangular cross windows, tall Gothic pointed blind-tympanum/cross windows, short rectangular top windows, blind tracery parapet, eleven stepped front dormers and eleven small red timber dormers on slate. Corner octagonal projecting turret/pierced gallery and crocketed spire. Apparent red/yellow shutters vary by era; selected2004–2018 appearance retained.

sources.inspection: Primary heritage record read: rectangular Tournai-limestone Gothic tower; three stages of paired pointed windows, seven stringcourses; twenty gargoyles/four watchmen, polygonal corner towers, lower gallery and open clock arches/upper gallery. Current stone crown1911–1913. Its1976scaffolding statement is historical, not current appearance. Dragon nearly3m long.

Primary record read: attached rectangular three-story Cloth Hall, eleven bays/eleven stepped dormers and eleven timber dormers each slope, four projecting octagonal corner turrets, slate gabled roof. South five-bay gable with split approach stair and Gothic portal. West side former jail annex retained. Current facade proportions estimated from photographs/native outline.
